issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an interface named Rideable (with method messageOnRide()), but the solution introduces a different interface name (Mountable) and has Pig and Seal implement Mountable. Additionally, Rideable.java in the solution is an empty file. This naming mismatch between Rideable (problem/template) and Mountable (solution) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about which interface to implement and which type Pig/Seal should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface naming across artifacts. Either rename Mountable in the solution to Rideable and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable, and ensure Rideable.java declares messageOnRide(); or update the problem statement/template to use Mountable consistently. Also remove or populate the empty Rideable.java in the solution to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to the ride-related interface as 'Rideable' (with method messageOnRide()), but the solution implementation defines/uses an interface named 'Mountable' and has Pig and Seal implement Mountable. This inconsistent identifier for the same concept (an animal that can be ridden) breaks the mapping between requirements/template code and the solution and will confuse students (and can cause compilation errors when following the template Main which expects Rideable).
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent interface name for the rideable concept across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Mountable' interface to 'Rideable' (or have 'Mountable' extend/alias 'Rideable') and update Pig and Seal to implement Rideable. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to use 'Mountable' everywhere. Prefer aligning the solution to the problem/template by replacing Mountable with Rideable and removing the conflicting empty Rideable.java placeholder.
